title: Subspace Optimization for Efficient Federated Learning under Heterogeneous Data
summary: Federated learning increasingly operates in a large-model regime where communication, memory, and computation are all scarce. Typically, non-IID client data induce drift that degrades the stability and performance of local training. Existing remedies such as SCAFFOLD introduce heterogeneity-correction mechanisms to address this challenge, but they incur substantial extra communication and memory overhead.
